data.summary: The client approved the design and the freelancer supplied a download link containing both web assets and a separate vector package, but the client never downloaded the vector files before the link expired, leaving them without the print‑ready assets they needed. Because the contract ties refund eligibility to delivery of the Final Asset Package, the dispute hinges on whether the unpaid vector files count as undelivered; the evidence shows a delivery attempt was made but the client did not retrieve the files, supporting the freelancer's position that delivery was fulfilled, though the client’s inability to use the assets gives them a partial merit claim.

data.rationale: The contract explicitly defines the Final Asset Package to include master vector source files and a print‑ready PDF (§3.2). The freelancer delivered a download link containing both the web/social pack and the master vectors zip (E6, L1). The client gave written approval of the final design on June 29 (E4, §5.1), which satisfies the acceptance condition. However, the delivery logs show zero downloads of the master vectors zip (L5) and the link expired without a re‑issue, leaving the client unable to use the brand assets. The client’s real problem is missing access to the master files, not a dispute over design quality. The contract also obligates the freelancer to re‑issue the package within 12 months on request (§7.2). Because the fee is non‑refundable after approval unless the Final Asset Package is not delivered, and the package was technically delivered (link sent), a full refund is not justified. Instead, we will contest the chargeback and immediately re‑issue the master files, satisfying the contract and fixing the client’s actual need.

evidences.notes:
The Agreement defines the Final Asset Package to include master vector source files and a print‑ready PDF. [1]

The client gave written approval of the final design on June 29, which meets the acceptance condition in the contract. [2][3]

On July 1, Priya sent a secure download link containing both the Web & Social pack and the Master Vectors zip, with a 30‑day expiration as stipulated. [4][5]

Download records show the Web & Social pack was downloaded on July 1 and July 9, but the Master Vectors zip recorded zero downloads before the link expired. [6][7][8][9]

Because the master vector files were never accessed, the client could not use the brand assets for print and signage, which is the actual problem reported. [10][8]

The contract obligates the studio to re‑issue the Final Asset Package at no charge within two business days upon request for up to twelve months after delivery. [11]

Fees are non‑refundable after written approval unless the studio fails to deliver the Final Asset Package; delivery was performed via the secure link, so a refund is not warranted. [12][5]

We are contesting the chargeback and will re‑issue a new secure download link with the master vector files and PDF within two business days, fulfilling the contractual re‑issue obligation. [11]

evidence_package.why: Shows contract terms for asset package contents, acceptance, non‑refund, and re‑issue obligations.

evidences.notes:
The Agreement defines the Final Asset Package to include master vector source files and a print‑ready PDF. [1]

The client gave written approval of the final design on June 29, which meets the acceptance condition in the contract. [2][3]

On July 1, Priya sent a secure download link containing both the Web & Social pack and the Master Vectors zip, with a 30‑day expiration as stipulated. [4][5]

Download records show the Web & Social pack was downloaded on July 1 and July 9, but the Master Vectors zip recorded zero downloads before the link expired. [6][7][8][9]

Because the master vector files were never accessed, the client could not use the brand assets for print and signage, which is the actual problem reported. [10][8]

The contract obligates the studio to re‑issue the Final Asset Package at no charge within two business days upon request for up to twelve months after delivery. [11]

Fees are non‑refundable after written approval unless the studio fails to deliver the Final Asset Package; delivery was performed via the secure link, so a refund is not warranted. [12][5]

We are contesting the chargeback and will re‑issue a new secure download link with the master vector files and PDF within two business days, fulfilling the contractual re‑issue obligation. [11]

body.message: Hi Daniel, I’m sorry you didn’t get the master files you need. I’ve just created a new secure link that includes the AI, SVG, EPS files and the print‑ready PDF, and you’ll receive it by email within the next few hours. Please let me know as soon as you’ve downloaded them or if anything else is missing. I’m here to make sure the brand assets work for your signage and vendors.

footnotes.quote: Final Asset Package: On completion Studio delivers a Final Asset Package containing: (a) a Web & Social pack of PNG and JPG files; (b) master vector source files in AI, SVG and EPS formats suitable for print, signage and merchandise; (c) a print‑ready PDF brand guide; and (d) a signed Assignment of Copyright letter.
Approval: This is it. Honestly better than I imagined. Approved, let's make it official. Send over the invoice and the final files!
Acceptance: Client's written approval of the final design (email is sufficient) constitutes acceptance of the design work.

Your Final Asset Package is ready as two downloads: (1) Halden_Web_Social_Pack.zip for your website, Instagram and menus, and (2) Halden_Master_Vectors_and_Copyright.zip with the AI/SVG/EPS master files for printers, sign makers and merch, the print brand guide, and your signed Assignment of Copyright. Please download both. Links stay active for 30 days.
